target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (T : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓢 T → Def2 𝓢 T → (∃ lam, 𝓢 ⊢ lam 🡘 T lam) → 𝓢 ⊢ ⊥
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition: for every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and of a provability relation for systems in S on sentences in Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, and every function T from Fm to Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication φ 🡒 T(φ); if also (2) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication T(φ) 🡒 φ; and if also (3) there exists a sentence lam such that 𝓢 proves the biconditional lam 🡘 T(lam), then 𝓢 proves ⊥. The biconditional in (3) relates lam to T(lam), not to its negation. Neither lam nor T(lam) is required to be provable on its own, and consistency of 𝓢 is not assumed."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition: for every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and of a provability relation for systems in S on sentences in Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, and every function T from Fm to Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication φ 🡒 T(φ); if also (2) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication T(φ) 🡒 φ; and if also (3) there exists a sentence lam such that 𝓢 proves the biconditional lam 🡘 T(lam), then 𝓢 proves ⊥. The biconditional in (3) relates lam to T(lam), not to its negation. Neither lam nor T(lam) is required to be provable on its own, and consistency of 𝓢 is not assumed.

divergences.description: The liar hypothesis needs `𝓢 ⊢ lam 🡘 ∼(T lam)`, but the target uses `𝓢 ⊢ lam 🡘 T lam`. This positive biconditional already follows for every sentence from T-In and T-Out. For example, taking `T` to be the identity in consistent classical propositional logic satisfies all three hypotheses without making `⊥` provable.

judgement.summary: The source states inconsistency after adding both T-In and K-Intro. The intended argument that T-In suffices in DTK uses T-Out and a liar without invoking K-Intro, but the missing negation makes the formal statement false.
